title: Turn-boundary-aware slab batcher with predictive KV hinge eviction
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background:
Streaming chat workloads have high variance in per-session token rates and frequent turn boundaries (user message -> assistant response). Current continuous batchers favor aggregation based on arrival time and size, which sometimes groups tokens across turn boundaries and increases tail latency when a user expects a low-latency assistant response.

Goal:
Design and implement a slab-based micro-batcher that is turn-boundary-aware and uses lightweight prediction signals to: 1) prioritize forming batches that complete at natural assistant-turn boundaries, 2) proactively manage GPU KV slots by 'hinge eviction' of low-value KV fragments to free contiguous slab space, and 3) reduce 99th/95th percentile latency while keeping token-cost overhead < 4%.

Approach / heuristics:
- Turn-boundary signals: use a compact in-request header (client-turn-id + tentative-response-length) and short-term session-level features (avg-turn-latency, recent inter-message gap) to score requests for turn-affinity.
- Soft-deadline buckets: assign each inflight request a soft deadline (ms) computed from its predicted remaining tokens and SLA tier; prioritize forming batches that allow earliest soft-deadline completions and avoid cross-turn hold-ups.
- Slab packing policy: maintain GPU memory as contiguous slabs (free-list). When incoming KV fragments would cause fragmentation that increases allocation failures, run a hinge-eviction pass that identifies low-reuse KV fragments (LRU-age, token-prefix-hit-rate) and coalesces their slots to form contiguous allocation units. Eviction is conservative and respects per-customer data retention constraints.
- Predictive prefetch/lock: for requests likely to extend (long assistant replies), pre-allocate a small contiguous KV reservation to avoid mid-generation compaction stalls; release if not used within a short timeout.
- Graceful preemption: if a high-priority turn arrives, allow in-progress micro-batches to be preempted and reassembled, moving partial KV state to a hot-cache region (fast-path) to minimize recompute.

Benchmarks / success metrics:
- Target: reduce streaming chat P95 latency by >= 20% and P99 by >= 15% under mixed PLG + enterprise traffic while keeping per-token cost delta <= +4% versus baseline batcher.
- Resource target: decrease fragmentation-induced allocation failures by >= 50% and reduce average KV compaction frequency by 40%.

Planned experiments:
1) Simulation harness: run on production request traces (anonymized) for 48h window; compare baseline, slab-only, slab+hinge-eviction, and slab+prediction variants. Measure latency percentiles, token cost, and GPU OOM/allocation failures.
2) Canary rollout: 1% of production traffic, runtime flag enable-turn-batcher; observe downstream SDK/backoff behavior and CPU overhead.
3) Incremental ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with rollback windows and built-in fallback to current batcher.

Implementation notes / milestones:
- Week 1: design doc and deterministic simulation harness (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/###).
- Week 2: implement slab allocator hooks + hinge-eviction pass; unit tests for eviction invariants.
- Week 3: implement turn-scoring and soft-deadline scheduler; integrate predictive prefetch.
- Week 4: internal perf run and canary.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: hinge-eviction might evict frequently reused KV leading to quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, offline A/B on eval prompt sets, and rollback by runtime flag.
- Risk: additional CPU overhead for scoring affects throughput. Mitigation: keep score computation O(1) using cached session stats and rate-limit scoring to new sessions.
- Risk: client integration (tentative-response-length) adoption lag. Mitigation: fallback to server-side heuristics using recent session lengths and inter-message gaps.

Acceptance criteria / definition of done:
- Simulation results show latency and fragmentation improvements against baseline per targets.
- Unit + integration tests covering allocator invariants, prefetch timeouts, and preemption flows.
- Canary run (>= 72h at 5% traffic) with no regressions in quality evals and acceptable cost delta (< +4%).
- Design doc and rollout plan reviewed and approved by Runtime and Platform SRE teams.
